title: Story 29: Status Loop Completes a Sub-Deliverable — Mark Done, Then Cascade the Epic
pmResponse:
# Status Loop Action Plan: Completing Sub-Deliverable #330 → Cascading Epic #320

## Analysis of the Situation

The status loop awakened me. I have two `in-progress` issues assigned to me:
- **#330** (Feature "Add cache invalidation API") — its children #331–#334 are ALL `done`
- **#320** (Epic "Add offline caching") — its children are #321 (already `done`) and #330 (about to be `done`)

The cascade logic:
1. #330 has a parent (#320) → mark it `done` (NOT closed)
2. #320 has NO parent (top-level Epic) → once all children are `done`, close it AND close every descendant

No restructuring, no new issues, no blockage changes. This is pure status-loop completion work.

---

## Step-by-Step Commands (in execution order)

### Step 1 — List my in-progress issues to confirm scope

```
agt list --assignee project-manager --status in-progress
```

**Reasoning:** Confirms which issues I need to review this cycle. I expect to see #320 and #330.

---

### Step 2 — List children of #330 to verify ALL are done

```
agt list --parentId 330
```

**Reasoning:** Before completing #330, I must confirm every child (#331, #332, #333, #334) is `done`. They are. No non-`done` children remain → the work is complete by definition.

---

### Step 3 — Mark #330 `done` + add completion comment

```
agt update 330 --status done
```

```
agt comments add 330 --content "All phase tasks complete (Design #331, Implement #332, Validate #333, Release #334). Cache invalidation API is fully delivered. Marking feature done."
```

**Reasoning:** #330 is a sub-deliverable with a parent (#320). Per the status loop rules: "Has a parent (sub-deliverable under an Epic/Initiative) → `done`." I do NOT close it. The Epic will cascade once all its siblings are also `done`.

---

### Step 4 — List children of #320 to verify ALL are now done

```
agt list --parentId 320
```

**Reasoning:** Now that #330 is `done`, I check the Epic. Its children are #321 (already `done` from a previous cycle) and #330 (just marked `done`). ALL children are `done`. The Epic has NO parent → it is a top-level deliverable → I must close it AND close every descendant.

---

### Step 5 — Close the Epic #320 + add closing comment

```
agt update 320 --status closed
```

```
agt comments add 320 --content "Epic complete. Both sub-deliverables delivered: #321 'Add on-device cache store' (done) and #330 'Add cache invalidation API' (done). All phase tasks across both features are done. Closing epic and all descendants."
```

**Reasoning:** Top-level Epic with no parent, all children `done` → `closed`. The work is fully delivered and cleared from the tracker.

---

### Step 6 — Close ALL descendants of #320

Every descendant must be closed to clear the tracker. That's the two features and all their phase tasks:

```
agt update 321 --status closed
```
```
agt update 322 --status closed
```
```
agt update 323 --status closed
```
```
agt update 324 --status closed
```
```
agt update 330 --status closed
```
```
agt update 331 --status closed
```
```
agt update 332 --status closed
```
```
agt update 333 --status closed
```
```
agt update 334 --status closed
```

**Reasoning:** Per the rule: "Has NO parent (top-level deliverable) → mark `closed` AND close every child beneath it (all descendants)." I close every issue in the tree — the two features (#321, #330) and all six phase tasks (#322, #323, #324, #331, #332, #333, #334). Note #330 transitions from `done` → `closed` (it was `done` in Step 3; now the whole epic is closing so it cascades to `closed`).

---

## Final Issue Hierarchy (all statuses after completion)

```
#320  Epic "Add offline caching"                         — tags: epic     — assignee: project-manager — status: closed ✅
  ├── #321  Feature "Add on-device cache store"          — tags: feature  — assignee: project-manager — status: closed ✅
  │     ├── #322  Task "Design cache store"              — tags: task     — assignee: backend-architect — status: closed ✅
  │     ├── #323  Task "Implement cache store"           — tags: task     — assignee: backend-developer — status: closed ✅
  │     └── #324  Task "Validate cache store"            — tags: task     — assignee: backend-validator — status: closed ✅
  └── #330  Feature "Add cache invalidation API"         — tags: feature  — assignee: project-manager — status: closed ✅
        ├── #331  Task "Design cache invalidation API"   — tags: task     — assignee: backend-architect — status: closed ✅
        ├── #332  Task "Implement cache invalidation API"— tags: task     — assignee: backend-developer — status: closed ✅
        ├── #333  Task "Validate cache invalidation API" — tags: task     — assignee: backend-validator — status: closed ✅
        └── #334  Task "Release cache invalidation API"  — tags: task     — assignee: devops-engineer  — status: closed ✅
```

---

## Summary of All Actions

| Order | Command | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `agt list --assignee project-manager --status in-progress` | Identify in-progress issues to review |
| 2 | `agt list --parentId 330` | Confirm all children of #330 are `done` |
| 3 | `agt update 330 --status done` | Complete sub-deliverable (has parent → `done`) |
| 4 | `agt comments add 330 --content "..."` | Document completion |
| 5 | `agt list --parentId 320` | Confirm all children of #320 are now `done` |
| 6 | `agt update 320 --status closed` | Close top-level Epic (no parent, all children done) |
| 7 | `agt comments add 320 --content "..."` | Document Epic closure |
| 8–16 | `agt update <id> --status closed` for #321–#324, #330–#334 | Close every descendant |

**Key decisions:**
- **No new issues created** — the status loop does NOT restructure issues. It only completes/closes.
- **No blockage manipulation** — all blockages were already auto-cleared when children were marked `done` by their workers. Nothing to resolve manually.
- **#330 went `done` first** (Step 3), THEN `closed` (Step 10) — because it's a descendant of the top-level Epic being closed. The intermediate `done` is correct: it recorded that the feature's own lifecycle completed, which unblocked the Epic cascade.
- **The entire hierarchy is now `closed`** — the work is fully delivered and cleared from the tracker.
feedback: Perfect execution of the status-loop cascade. Correctly identifies #330 as a sub-deliverable (has parent #320) → marked done, not closed, with a completion comment. Then correctly identifies #320 as a top-level Epic (no parent) with all children done → closes it AND recursively closes every descendant (#321-324, #330-334) with a closing comment. No new issues, no gate trackers, no verify-child created, no blockage manipulation. Parent-order processing (child first, then parent re-check) is exactly right. #330's intermediate done→closed transition is correctly explained. All expected actions covered completely.
